newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia economy mixed, parts flat - Howard.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia economy mixed, parts flat - Howard.

text.p: The Australian economy was mixed, with some areas including the manufacturing sector flat, Prime Minister John Howard told Perth radio.
He had been asked about interest rates and whether the economy was weak.
"The economy is mixed. There are some areas that are flat, some areas of manufacturing are flat," Howard said.
"Parts of the service industries are good; there are some signs of a housing and construction recovery but areas of manufacturing are flat and retailing, to say the least, is modest," he said.

Asked about the possibility of the Reserve Bank cutting interest rates following its monthly board meeting today, Howard said, "If the Senate passed our budget intact that would help the interest rate climate."
"Having said all of that prime ministers always like to see low interest rates, but what happens with monetary policy is ultimately a matter for the Reserve Bank," he said.

Asked about claims that the economy was weak and a rate cut was needed, Howard said: "The things that drive interes rate levels are myriad -- the level of inflation, the rate of wage increases, as well as activity and views about employment."

"They are all things that have to be taken into account and I don't think it probably helps the process of orderly decision making for me to be talking about what ought to happen with interest rates tomorrow," Howard said.
On Monday, opposition Labor Treasury spokesman Gareth Evans said it was clear economic activity was very subdued and the Reserve Bank should cut interest rates immediately to kickstart jobs growth.
Official cash rates were last cut by 50 basis points to 7.0 percent on July 31.
